lectures.title: Using Curly Braces & Understanding the Core Syntax

cues.en: Back in our project, I made one tiny change.
Attached to this lecture you find a new global CSS file which you should download and simply replace
the content in your existing global CSS file with this content.
You can leave the rest as it is, and once you did this, restart this server with NPM run dev.
Then on localhost 5000 you should see something like this.
So some new styles and if you don't see that, open your developer tools in the browser and then right
click on that refresh icon here in Chrome and click empty cache and hard reload or do it in whichever
browser you are using to make sure you're fetching the latest version of our code.
So with this you should see this output here.
And of course that is only well content you saw before just styled a bit differently.
But now let me dig into that syntax we were using and let me explain what's happening there and which
other features Svelte has.
I already mentioned that these curly brace things here in the svelte files in the markup set up, you
could say live connections between this place in your HTML code, in your Dom and the respective variables
you have in your script tag.
So name here between the curly braces in the markup refers to the name variable and the same is true
for age and increment age.
The function here.
And that indeed is probably the core mechanism of svelte.
It has many other features built in that help you with building modern web applications and with managing
your data efficiently and so on.
But when it comes to outputting content, that really is the core curly braces, single curly braces
in your markup are recognized by the svelte compiler and they tell Svelte that it should look for something
named like the content between the curly braces is in your script tags.
So here it looks for something named name and it finds this variable.
Here it looks for something named age and it finds this variable and it finds something named increment
age.
This function and then svelte establishes a connection.
And if you just have curly braces like this, which you have here in some text, and I will later also
show you how to assign values to attributes and properties.
If you have it here, then Svelte will automatically look for a value it can output here.
So when you're using it like this name and age, you should always refer to a variable or something
related that can be output as text here.
Now it automatically, as you see here, at the example of age.
Transforms this number to text so you can directly output numbers here.
You don't need to transform this manually.
When you're pointing at a function, it doesn't automatically execute that function for you.
That only works here when you click the button because we decorated this with this on colon Click annotation.
This is not a built in HTML attribute.
Of course, this is instead some syntax which would normally be ignored by the browser because it's
not understood by the browser out of the box.
Instead, this is syntax understood by svelte and it tells svelte to add an event listener to the button
which should eventually trigger increment age when well this executes.
It is worth pointing out that on click and on whatever event you're listening to, of course you're
not limited to click.
You can listen to any event.
An HTML element supports whatever you're listening to.
You always have to pass a pointer and a function here between the curly braces.
When outputting text like here, you always have to reference something or point at something that holds
a value that can be output.
Now you can add any JavaScript expression between these curly braces, any single line expression.
So you can also, for example, output H plus one here that would also be valid.
You're not restricted to a single variable.
You can have any simple JavaScript expression here, no complex for loop or if statement, but a one
line expression like this will work.
And now you see H is 31 here, even though I haven't clicked the button and H is 30 at the start because
I'm adding one here now.
This can be very convenient.
You can also do things like name to uppercase.
Make sure you get the casing of that command right.
To transform Max to uppercase Max because to uppercase is normal JavaScript syntax.
You can call this method on a string and name is just a string to transform it to uppercase.
So that all works.
But most of the time you should keep your markup code here relatively lean and not do complex calculations
in there, but instead try to really only output single values.
And if you have values that have to be derived based on other values.
So if you want to transform this to uppercase, then you should instead do it up here in the script
tags and there is a convenient syntax svelte gives you which helps you with that.
